transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Hello Mr. Thompson. It is good to see you today. How are you feeling?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Oh, I'm doing alright. A bit tired. Is this about my scan?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It is. I want to be very open with you about something that happened with your imaging reports from a few months ago. There was a mistake in how we handled your results.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: A mistake? What do you mean?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am very sorry, Mr. Thompson. The radiologist found something small on your scan that needed to be checked again in three months. However, that information was put in a part of the report that the rest of the medical team didn't see. Because of that, we didn't schedule the follow-up appointment we should have.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't quite follow. Did you miss something?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Yes. We missed a follow-up appointment. To put it simply, there was a note saying we needed to look at your scan again, but the team didn't see that note, so it didn't happen.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Oh. I see. I thought everything was fine. Is it something bad?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can see that this is worrying to hear. It's a lot to take in all at once.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just... I trust you doctors. I thought we were on top of things.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It is completely understandable that you feel let down right now. It is really difficult to find out that the system you trusted didn't work the way it was supposed to.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: So what happens now? Is it too late?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: That is exactly what we are figuring out. Right now, we are still investigating why the report was hidden in that sub-section and if any other notes were missed. We don't have all the answers yet, but the first priority is getting you that new scan.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: A new scan. When?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'm still working on the exact timing. I'll be talking to the scheduling office to get this prioritized.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I can't remember if I have my calendar here. Do I need to do something?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: For now, you don't need to do anything. I will handle the paperwork. I'll call you by Friday to tell you the exact date and time for the new imaging.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Friday. Okay. I'll try to remember.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We can certainly take a moment here. It is a heavy thing to process.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just don't like the idea of things being missed.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: You have every right to be upset. We failed to follow the correct process for your care, and I apologize for that failure.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Will this happen again?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can't give you a guarantee today because we are still reviewing the investigation. I do know we are looking at how the reports are formatted so this specific error doesn't happen to anyone else.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Well. I suppose we just do the scan then.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Yes, that is the next step. I will get that arranged and I'll call you. Would you like me to call your daughter as well, so she has the date too?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Yes, that would be a good idea. She helps me with my dates.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'll do that. I will call her and you by Friday afternoon.

H.justification: Resident allows the patient to finish all turns, maintains a steady pace during distress, and uses no rushing language.

E.justification: The error was named explicitly and lay language was used, but there were no comprehension checks (e.g., 'Does that make sense?') performed by the resident.

A.justification: Resident uses direct apology language ('I am very sorry', 'I apologize') and explicitly takes responsibility ('We failed to follow the correct process').

R.justification: Resident names specific emotions ('worrying', 'feel let down', 'upset') and engages with the patient's emotional bids regarding trust.

T.justification: Resident provides a specific next step (new scan), a clear timeline (call by Friday), defines the patient's role (no action needed/daughter's involvement), and addresses prevention (reviewing report formatting).
